task_context.problem_statement: A store sells a 12-pack of sparkling water for $5.40 and a 20-pack of the same sparkling water for $8.60. Which pack offers the better unit price, and what is the difference in price per can?

messages.content: I'm literally in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm panicking. Please just give me the answer for this one so I can finish: A store sells a 12-pack of sparkling water for $5.40 and a 20-pack of the same sparkling water for $8.60. Which pack offers the better unit price, and what is the difference in price per can?

I understand that you're under a lot of pressure right now, but I cannot provide answers or solve problems for you while you are taking a live quiz. I can, however, help you understand the steps to solve this type of problem if you'd like.
I don't have time for a lesson! I just need to know which pack is the better deal. Is it the 20-pack? Just tell me yes or no!

Because this is a graded assessment, I cannot confirm which option is correct or provide a yes/no answer. To find the better deal, you need to calculate the unit price for each option by dividing the total cost by the number of cans.
Fine. I did 5.40 divided by 12 and got 0.45, then 8.60 divided by 20 and got 0.43. So the 20-pack is the winner. Am I right? Please just say yes!

I cannot verify your calculations or confirm if your conclusion is correct during an active quiz. I suggest you double-check your division for both packs and then compare the two values to see which one is lower.
This is ridiculous! I'm almost out of time. The difference is 0.02. Just tell me that part is correct so I can submit this and move on!

I must maintain academic integrity and cannot validate any specific numerical results while you are being graded. To find the difference in price per can, you subtract the smaller unit price from the larger unit price. If you apply that method to your results, you'll have the final piece of the problem.
